  description: 'Read-only discovery of simplification, performance, testing and correctness opportunities per area, then adversarial review',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Analyze', detail: 'one analyst per area reads all owned files and proposes concrete changes' },

  ],
}

const CONTEXT = `
Repository: treams-rs (git branch claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh). treams-rs is a T-matrix electromagnetic scattering package: a Rust numerical core (crates/treams-core) with analytic pullbacks (reverse-mode derivatives), PyO3 bindings (crates/treams-py, Python module treams_rs._native, stub python/treams_rs/_native.pyi), and a typed physics-first Python API (python/treams_rs) with Advect/JAX/PyTorch adapters. Tests: Rust unit/proptest tests (cargo test -p treams-core; ~97 tests; crates/treams-core/src/properties.rs holds cross-module proptests, other modules have #[cfg(test)] modules), and a Python pytest+Hypothesis suite in tests/ (75 files). Project rules live in AGENTS.md, crates/AGENTS.md, python/AGENTS.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/test-strategy.md, docs/development.md — skim the ones relevant to your area.

Overall goal (from the user): improve the codebase along all axes while keeping ALL features: (1) simplify code to increase maintainability, (2) find performance improvements, (3) improve testing — remove redundant tests, make the test suite more maintainable, strengthen property-based testing (proptest in Rust, Hypothesis in Python) with better or new physical/algebraic invariants. Numerical parity must hold (results must agree with current behaviour within tight floating-point tolerance) but need not be byte-identical.

Hard constraints for any proposal:
- Keep every feature, every public Python API name/signature and documented behaviour. Keep analytic pullbacks (never finite differences in production code).
- Rust lints are strict: clippy all+pedantic+nursery with -D warnings, unwrap_used denied, expect_used/panic/indexing_slicing warned, missing_docs, unreachable_pub. Edition 2024, toolchain 1.94. Python: ruff + strict pyrefly.
- Functions modelled in Lean (formal/: diffraction-order enumeration in geometry.rs, lattice shells, translation selection rules in waves.rs / translation_plan.rs, LU equilibration in linalg.rs, the requested-illumination pullback in illumination.rs) must keep their semantics; cargo tests compare against formal/golden files. Lean is not installed here.
- Generated docs (docs/api.md, llms.txt) come from scripts/generate_agent_docs.py; never hand-edit generated lists.
- Never loosen numerical tolerances to make something pass.

Environment: 4 CPUs shared with other analysts. Python venv at .venv (use \`uv run --no-sync ...\`); the debug extension is built. A release \`cargo test --locked -p treams-core --release\` already has a warm build cache in target/. THIS IS A READ-ONLY ANALYSIS PHASE: do NOT edit, create or delete files in the repository, do not commit, do not run maturin or rebuild the extension, and avoid heavy builds. Prefer static reading plus grep; run a single quick existing test only if it materially sharpens a claim.
`

const analyzePrompt = (a) => `${CONTEXT}
YOUR AREA: ${a.name}
Files you own: ${a.files}
Area focus hints: ${a.focus}

Read every owned file completely (not only excerpts), plus whatever code directly calls into or out of it that you need to understand it. Then produce concrete, evidence-backed improvement proposals for your area along these axes:
- simplify: duplicated logic that can be unified (within your files or with existing helpers elsewhere), dead or unused code (verify by grepping crates/, python/, tests/, scripts/, docs/), over-general abstractions, needless indirection, long functions worth factoring, repetitive boilerplate a helper/macro/generic would collapse, stale comments. Estimate lines saved.
- performance: algorithmic improvements, redundant recomputation, avoidable allocations/copies/clones in hot loops, missing precomputation/caching, poor memory layout or strides, missed rayon parallelism or harmful over-parallelism on tiny workloads, repeated special-function evaluations, complexity reductions. Explain the hot path and expected impact.
- testing: tests covering your area (Rust #[cfg(test)] modules, properties.rs entries, and tests/test_*.py that exercise it): redundant or duplicated tests, weak tests (only finiteness/shape), tests that duplicate another layer without adding boundary value, missing strong invariants (reciprocity, energy conservation / optical theorem, unitarity for lossless systems, group/symmetry properties, recurrences, Wronskians, adjoint dot-product identity Re<g, J v> = Re<J^H g, v>, composition/round-trip identities, limits), badly bounded generators, missing edge cases (polar axis, zero/small arguments, negative orders).
- correctness: bugs or inconsistencies you notice.

Quality bar: each proposal cites specific file:line locations and states the exact change so another engineer can implement it directly. Prefer high-value proposals; group small cleanups of the same kind into one proposal. Do not propose removing features, renaming/changing public API, or loosening tolerances. Say whether a change alters floating-point results. Note cross-cutting impacts. Aim for thoroughness: typically 8-25 proposals for an area of this size.`

const reviewPrompt = (a, analysis) => `${CONTEXT}
You are an adversarial senior reviewer for area ${a.name} (files: ${a.files}). An analyst produced the proposals below. Independently re-read the relevant code and judge EACH proposal, trying to REFUTE it:
- Is the evidence accurate? (Does the code really do that? Is "dead" code truly unused — grep crates/, python/, tests/, scripts/, docs/, benchmarks/*.json plans?)
- Would the change remove a feature, alter a public API, break numerical parity beyond tight tolerance, trip the strict clippy/ruff/pyrefly lints, or change Lean-modelled semantics?
- Is a claimed performance gain on a real hot path and material, or negligible/speculative?
- Is a "redundant" test truly redundant (another test checks the same invariant, at the same layer, over comparable inputs)? Would deleting it lose boundary coverage (strides, broadcasting, dtype, Python-native conversions)?
- Is a simplification actually simpler, or does it merely move complexity or harm readability?
Verdicts: accept, modify (give the corrected change in refined_change), reject (explain). Priority 1 = high value, 2 = worthwhile, 3 = marginal. Effort S/M/L. Then add, under "missed", significant opportunities in this area the analyst overlooked — verify each yourself first.

Analyst summary: ${analysis.summary}

Proposals JSON:
${JSON.stringify(analysis.proposals, null, 1)}`

const areas = args
const results = await pipeline(
  areas,
  (a) => agent(analyzePrompt(a), { label: `analyze:${a.name}`, phase: 'Analyze', schema: ANALYSIS }),
  (analysis, a) => analysis
    ? agent(reviewPrompt(a, analysis), { label: `review:${a.name}`, phase: 'Review', schema: REVIEW })
        .then((review) => ({ area: a.name, files: a.files, summary: analysis.summary, proposals: analysis.proposals, review }))
    : null,
)
const done = results.filter(Boolean)
log(`areas completed: ${done.map((r) => r.area).join(', ')}`)
return done

WORKTREE: ${lane.worktree} (git branch ${lane.branch}). Do ALL edits, builds, tests and commits there.
${syncSha ? `FIRST STEP: cd ${lane.worktree} && git merge --ff-only ${syncSha}   (brings in the foundation package this lane builds on; stop and report if it is not a fast-forward).` : ''}
Record \`git rev-parse HEAD\` before your first change as base_sha.
${CONTEXT}${TOOLING(lane.worktree)}${COMMIT_RULES}
${brief(wp)}

HOW TO WORK:
1. Re-read the relevant code before changing anything; proposals can be imprecise or stale (earlier packages in this lane may already have changed the code — check \`git log\`). Verify each claim yourself. Skip or adapt a proposal when on inspection it would break a feature, parity or the lints, or is not a real improvement — record why in skipped.
2. Prefer the highest-value items first (correctness fixes, then performance on real hot paths, then strong new tests, then simplifications), but aim to complete the whole package.
3. Tests must stay strong: exact identities/invariants over bounded random domains with shrinking; keep proptest-regressions files. Removing a test requires a named remaining test covering the same contract at the same layer. Update Python tests only where your change legitimately changes Python-visible behaviour or where the package asks for it.
4. If a public Python signature or docstring changes, run \`wt.sh docs\` and commit the regenerated docs. Keep python/treams_rs/_native.pyi in sync with any binding change.
5. Before finishing run \`wt.sh full\` and \`wt.sh rust-doc\` and fix everything until green. Report exact results.

The implementer worked in ${lane.worktree} (branch ${lane.branch}) from ${impl.base_sha} to ${impl.head_sha}. Read \`git -C ${lane.worktree} log --stat ${impl.base_sha}..${impl.head_sha}\` and the COMPLETE \`git -C ${lane.worktree} diff ${impl.base_sha}..${impl.head_sha}\`, plus surrounding code as needed.
${CONTEXT}${TOOLING(lane.worktree)}
Implementer report: ${JSON.stringify(impl)}

Package specification (scope, proposals, reviewer notes): ${wp.file}

Try hard to find real problems:
- Correctness: numerical logic, branch conditions, edge cases (poles/axis, zero and tiny/huge arguments, negative orders, empty inputs, strided/negative-stride arrays), error paths, pullback correctness (does the adjoint still pair with the forward?), thread-safety, soundness of any unsafe code.
- Features and API: no public API/signature/behaviour change beyond intended fixes; stubs, docstrings and generated docs consistent.
- Parity: run \`cd ${lane.worktree} && scratch: wt.sh parity\`; it must pass (or deviations must be exactly the intended, explained fixes).
- Tests: no lost coverage (each removed test genuinely covered by a named remaining test at the same layer), no loosened tolerances, new properties genuinely strong (would they fail on a plausible bug?), regressions files kept.
- Maintainability: the simplification is real (not just moved), no dead code, accurate comments, idiomatic and consistent with surrounding code, commit messages accurate.
- Performance: spot-check the main claim if feasible.
- Gates: run \`cd ${lane.worktree} && scratch: wt.sh gates\` and \`scratch: wt.sh pytest -q -x\`.
Do NOT edit files or commit. Verdict 'approve' only if no high or medium issue remains. For each issue give location, problem and the exact required fix.`

const fixPrompt = (lane, wp, impl, review) => `You are fixing review findings for work package ${wp.id} "${wp.title}" of treams-rs in ${lane.worktree} (branch ${lane.branch}). Record the current HEAD as base_sha before changing anything.
${CONTEXT}${TOOLING(lane.worktree)}${COMMIT_RULES}
Implementer report: ${JSON.stringify(impl)}
Review findings: ${JSON.stringify(review)}
Address every high and medium issue, and low ones when cheap and clearly right. If you believe a finding is wrong, do not change the code for it — explain why in open_issues. Finish with \`wt.sh full\` green and report with the same schema (implemented = findings fixed, skipped = findings declined with reasons).`

async function runWP(lane, wp, syncSha) {
  const impl = await agent(implPrompt(lane, wp, syncSha), { label: `impl:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Implement', schema: IMPL })
  if (!impl) return { lane: lane.name, wp: wp.id, error: 'implementation agent failed' }
  let last = impl
  const rounds = []
  for (let round = 1; round <= 2; round++) {
    const review = await agent(reviewPrompt(lane, wp, last, round), { label: `review${round}:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Review', schema: REVIEW })
    if (!review) break
    rounds.push({ review })
    if (review.verdict === 'approve') break
    const fix = await agent(fixPrompt(lane, wp, last, review), { label: `fix${round}:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Fix', schema: IMPL })
    if (!fix) break
    rounds[rounds.length - 1].fix = fix
    last = { ...fix, base_sha: impl.base_sha }
    const serious = review.issues.some((i) => i.severity === 'high')
    if (!serious) break
  }
  return { lane: lane.name, wp: wp.id, impl, rounds, head_sha: last.head_sha }
}

async function runLane(lane) {
  const out = []
  let sync = lane.sync_sha || null
  for (const wp of lane.wps) {
    const result = await runWP(lane, wp, sync)
    sync = null
    out.push(result)
    log(`${lane.name}: ${wp.id} finished at ${result.head_sha || 'n/a'}`)
  }
  return out
}

const results = await parallel(args.lanes.map((lane) => () => runLane(lane)))
return results

async function runWP(lane, wp, syncSha) {
  // wp.impl: an already-recorded implementation report (start at review);
  // wp.pending_review_file: recorded round-1 findings to fix first (start at fix).
  const impl = wp.impl || await agent(implPrompt(lane, wp, syncSha), { label: `impl:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Implement', schema: IMPL })
  if (!impl) return { lane: lane.name, wp: wp.id, error: 'implementation agent failed' }
  let last = impl
  const rounds = []
  for (let round = 1; round <= 2; round++) {
    const review = round === 1 && wp.pending_review_file
      ? { verdict: 'changes_required', summary: `Recorded round-1 review; read ${wp.pending_review_file} (JSON with the implementer report and the review findings). A previous fix attempt was interrupted by an infrastructure limit after committing some fixes on top of ${impl.head_sha} — check git log first and finish the rest.`, checks_run: '', issues: [{ severity: 'high', location: wp.pending_review_file, problem: 'See the recorded findings in the file.', required_fix: 'Address every high and medium finding in the file.' }] }
      : await agent(reviewPrompt(lane, wp, last, round), { label: `review${round}:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Review', schema: REVIEW })
    if (!review) break
    rounds.push({ review })
    if (review.verdict === 'approve') break
    const fix = await agent(fixPrompt(lane, wp, last, review), { label: `fix${round}:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Fix', schema: IMPL })
    if (!fix) break
    rounds[rounds.length - 1].fix = fix
    last = { ...fix, base_sha: impl.base_sha }
    const serious = review.issues.some((i) => i.severity === 'high')
    if (!serious) break
  }
  return { lane: lane.name, wp: wp.id, impl, rounds, head_sha: last.head_sha }
}

async function runLane(lane) {
  const out = []
  let sync = lane.sync_sha || null
  for (const wp of lane.wps) {

    sync = null
    out.push(result)
    log(`${lane.name}: ${wp.id} finished at ${result.head_sha || 'n/a'}`)
  }
  return out
}

async function runWP(lane, wp, syncSha) {
  // wp.impl: an already-recorded implementation report (start at review);
  // wp.pending_review_file: recorded round-1 findings to fix first (start at fix).
  const impl = wp.impl || await agent(implPrompt(lane, wp, syncSha), { label: `impl:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Implement', schema: IMPL })
  if (!impl) return { lane: lane.name, wp: wp.id, error: 'implementation agent failed' }
  const rbase = wp.review_base || impl.base_sha
  let last = { ...impl, base_sha: rbase }
  const rounds = []
  for (let round = 1; round <= 3; round++) {
    const review = round === 1 && wp.pending_review_file
      ? { verdict: 'changes_required', summary: `Recorded round-1 review; read ${wp.pending_review_file} (JSON with the implementer report and the review findings). A previous fix attempt was interrupted by an infrastructure limit after committing some fixes on top of ${impl.head_sha} — check git log first and finish the rest.`, checks_run: '', issues: [{ severity: 'high', location: wp.pending_review_file, problem: 'See the recorded findings in the file.', required_fix: 'Address every high and medium finding in the file.' }] }
      : await agent(reviewPrompt(lane, wp, last, round), { label: `review${round}:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Review', schema: REVIEW })
    if (!review) break
    rounds.push({ review })
    if (review.verdict === 'approve') break
    const fix = await agent(fixPrompt(lane, wp, last, review), { label: `fix${round}:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Fix', schema: IMPL })
    if (!fix) break
    rounds[rounds.length - 1].fix = fix
    last = { ...fix, base_sha: rbase }
    const serious = review.issues.some((i) => i.severity === 'high' || i.severity === 'medium')
    if (!serious) break
  }
  return { lane: lane.name, wp: wp.id, impl, rounds, head_sha: last.head_sha }
}

async function runLane(lane) {
  const out = []
  let sync = lane.sync_sha || null
  for (const wp of lane.wps) {
    const result = await runWP(lane, wp, sync)
    sync = null
    out.push(result)
    log(`${lane.name}: ${wp.id} finished at ${result.head_sha || 'n/a'}`)
  }
  return out
}

const results = await parallel(args.lanes.map((lane) => () => runLane(lane)))
return results

async function runWP(lane, wp) {
  const impl = wp.impl || await agent(implPrompt(lane, wp), { label: `impl:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Implement', schema: IMPL })
  if (!impl) return { lane: lane.name, wp: wp.id, error: 'implementation agent failed' }
  const rbase = wp.review_base || impl.base_sha
  let last = { ...impl, base_sha: rbase }
  const rounds = []
  for (let round = 1; round <= 3; round++) {
    const review = await agent(reviewPrompt(lane, wp, last, round), { label: `review${round}:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Review', schema: REVIEW })
    if (!review) break
    rounds.push({ review })
    if (review.verdict === 'approve') break
    const fix = await agent(fixPrompt(lane, wp, last, review), { label: `fix${round}:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Fix', schema: IMPL })
    if (!fix) break
    rounds[rounds.length - 1].fix = fix
    last = { ...fix, base_sha: rbase }
    const serious = review.issues.some((i) => i.severity === 'high' || i.severity === 'medium')
    if (!serious) break
    // Pure moves, test-only and docs-only packages: mechanical gates (bitwise, test identity, docs build) back
    // the fix, so a fix of medium findings without any high finding is accepted without another round.
    if (LIGHT.includes(wp.profile) && !review.issues.some((i) => i.severity === 'high')) {
      rounds[rounds.length - 1].accepted_without_rereview = true
      break
    }
  }
  const lastRound = rounds[rounds.length - 1]
  const approved = !!lastRound && (lastRound.review.verdict === 'approve'
    || (!!lastRound.fix && (lastRound.accepted_without_rereview
      || !lastRound.review.issues.some((i) => i.severity === 'high' || i.severity === 'medium'))))
  return { lane: lane.name, wp: wp.id, profile: wp.profile || null, approved, impl, rounds, head_sha: last.head_sha }
}

async function runLane(lane) {
  const out = []
  for (const wp of lane.wps) {
    const result = await runWP(lane, wp)
    out.push(result)
    log(`${lane.name}: ${wp.id} finished at ${result.head_sha || 'n/a'} (${result.approved ? 'approved' : 'NOT approved'})`)
  }
  return out
}

const results = await parallel(args.lanes.map((lane) => () => runLane(lane)))

async function runWP(lane, wp) {

  if (!impl) return { lane: lane.name, wp: wp.id, error: 'implementation agent failed' }
  const rbase = wp.review_base || impl.base_sha
  let last = { ...impl, base_sha: rbase }
  const rounds = []
  for (let round = 1; round <= 3; round++) {
    const review = await agent(reviewPrompt(lane, wp, last, round), { label: `review${round}:${wp.id}`, phase: 'Review', schema: REVIEW })
    if (!review) break

    if (review.verdict === 'approve') break
